candidates.title: Piraeus container throughput returns to growth in third quarter
candidates.excerpt: Container throughput at Pier I of the Port of Piraeus returned to growth during the third quarter of 2026, despite remaining significantly lower across the first nine months of the year. Piraeus Port Authority (PPA) said third-quarter throughput at Pier I increased by 0.3%, or 524 TEUs, compared with the same period in 2025. This marked the terminal’s first positive quarterly performance of 2026. Volumes improved more strongly during August and September, rising by 11.5%, or 10,161 TEUs. PPA attributed the recovery partly to new container-handling agreements with Piraeus Container Terminal and Pier I’s main customer. The agreements took retroactive effect from July and include revised tariffs and handling volumes. During October, Pier I handled five additional containerships and 7,843 TEUs under the agreement with Piraeus Container Terminal. candidates.excerpt: Cameroon’s Gulfcam is pursuing plans to acquire six vessels to expand its coastal container shipping operations between Kribi and Douala, with a former Camship executive taking charge of the business. Bernard André Ndengue took over as chief executive on November 1, replacing Albert Roger Boum, who stepped down last month to head Puma Energy’s operations in the Republic of Congo. Ndengue, a veteran of the country’s maritime sector who previously held senior positions at Cameroon Shipping Lines (Camship), has been tasked with developing Gulfcam’s container shipping arm and pushing ahead with its coastal shipping ambitions. The Douala-based group outlined plans in March to acquire six vessels to increase capacity between Cameroon’s two main ports, with the aim of capturing around half of the container freight currently transported by road along the corridor. candidates.title: Yet another strong month for alternative-fuel vessel orders – DNV
candidates.excerpt: Yet another strong month for alternative-fuel vessel orders – DNV DNV’s Alternative Fuels Insight (AFI) platform recorded 53 alternative-fuelled vessel orders in October, according to DNV senior consultant Kristian Hammer. The latest orders followed 69 vessels recorded in September, with LNG maintaining its lead among alternative marine fuels. LNG-capable vessels made up 30 orders in October, down from 48 in September. Container ships led the LNG segment with 18 orders, followed by car carriers with 12. A total of 230 LNG-capable vessels were ordered in the first 10 months of 2026, with the fuel now representing around 64% of all alternative-fuelled vessel orders this year. “Container ships account for 134 of these and car carriers for 75, meaning the two segments together represent 90% of LNG orders so far in 2026,” Hammer said. candidates.title: First look: CPKC earnings
candidates.excerpt: Canadian Pacific Kansas City reported a 16% increase in third-quarter core adjusted earnings per share Wednesday, as higher freight volumes and growth in grain and intermodal revenue helped offset rising fuel costs. Revenue rose to C$4.22 billion ($3.01 billion) in the three months ended Sept. 30 from $2.61 billion a year earlier, the Calgary-based company (NYSE: CP) said in earnings released after the close of markets. Core adjusted diluted earnings increased to 91 cents per share from 78 cents, while reported diluted earnings rose 3% to 74 cents from 72 cents. candidates.title: Greenbrier profit falls as railcar demand weighs on sales
candidates.excerpt: Greenbrier Cos. reported a sharp decline in quarterly profit and revenue as the freight-railcar manufacturer contended with weaker demand and facility-related costs. The Lake Oswego, Ore., company (NYSE: GBX) saw an increase in its order backlog and growth in its leasing fleet amid improving business conditions. The company said Monday that net earnings attributable to Greenbrier fell to $8.7 million, or 27 cents a diluted share, in its fiscal fourth quarter ended Aug. 31, from $36.8 million, or $1.16 a share, a year earlier. Revenue declined 22% to $591 million from $759.5 million. Excluding facility-rationalization costs, core earnings were 39 cents a share. The charges reduced quarterly earnings by 12 cents a share after tax and non-controlling interests. Revenue fell short of analysts’ expectations of about $605 million, while core earnings missed the 80-cent analysts’ consensus of MarketBeat.
